nodes.text: 2o7 explores Kenya's 2007–08 post-election period. It contains themes of political tension, ethnic division, displacement, and loss. Player discretion is advised.
Early morning. A single-room house in the estate. Clothes folded on a chair. A calendar on the wall reads DECEMBER 2006. Radio murmurs from next door.

nodes.speaker: mum
nodes.text: {player_name}, uko tayari? Bus ya Gikomba haingojangi mtu.
nodes.gloss: {player_name}, are you ready? The Gikomba bus doesn't wait for anyone.

nodes.text: She's at the table, counting coins from a faded purse. Two piles — one bigger, one small. She pushes the small pile towards you.

nodes.speaker: mum
nodes.text: Hii ni ya matatu — kwenda na kurudi. Usipoteze.
nodes.gloss: This is for the matatu — to and from. Don't lose it.

nodes.speaker: mum
nodes.text: Na ukifika kwa Mama Achieng', behave. She's a good woman. Don't be making jokes about her kiosk.

choices.text: When am I ever not good?

nodes.speaker: mum
nodes.gloss: Mm. Go well. God bless you.

nodes.speaker: mum
nodes.text: Eeh? Just last week you told Mama Njeri her chapatis taste like cardboard. Go. Behave.
You step outside. The estate is waking up — water drums, radio static, someone's rooster that never shuts up. The sun is already warm on your neck.
You walk the familiar path to Stage 7. Past the fundis welding jua kali, past the mama mboga with her tomato pyramids, past the kids kicking a ball made of plastic bags.
nodes.gloss: fundis = craftsmen, jua kali = informal sector, mama mboga = vegetable seller

nodes.text: Stage 7. The matatu terminus. Touts yelling destinations, exhaust fumes, bright paint jobs. You spot a familiar matatu — MSAFIRI, painted electric blue with a giant Nonini mural on the side.
